title: Fix punctuation bug in wordstat.count_words/word_freq

mutations.desc: naive fix that only strips edge punctuation per whitespace token (still wrong for hyphens/inner punctuation) must be caught by the test suite
counting unique tokens instead of all tokens must be caught

prompt: The project in this workspace is a tiny text-stats library `wordstat`. BUG: `wordstat.counter.count_words` uses `str.split()`, but the documented contract says a word is a maximal run of ASCII alphanumerics [A-Za-z0-9]; every other character (punctuation, apostrophes, symbols) is a separator. So '... wait -- what?!' must count 2 words (wait, what), 'state-of-the-art' must count 4, and pure noise counts 0. `wordstat.stats.word_freq` inherits the same bug via edge-stripping. TASK: fix `wordstat/counter.py` and `wordstat/stats.py` so ALL tests pass, including `tests/test_counter.py` which currently fails. Rules: do NOT rename files/packages/functions; do NOT edit or delete tests; keep the public API (`count_words`, `word_freq`) behavior-compatible with the docstrings. Verify with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` (or plain `python -m pytest`) inside the workspace.
